title: Extra Chapter: Alternate Account—Tatezaburō’s Journey to the East
text: My name is Naofumi Iwatani. One day, while I was browsing through light novels at the library, I came across a book called *The Book of the Four Holy Weapons*. As I was reading it, I found myself in a dream-like situation where I was summoned to another world as the Shield Hero—a character from the book—and that’s how I ended up living as a hero in this other world. So, after all sorts of adventures in this new world, I was resting at an inn with my heart full of anticipation when… I heard a knock-knock on the door, so I decided to answer it.
“Yes?”
“Naofumi Iwatani-kun. Pardon me for disturbing you so late at night, pyon.”

A visitor who knows my name? Who could it be? Maybe the king, or someone sent by the kingdom—something like that? Still, “pyon” is a pretty unusual way to end a sentence… When I opened the door, there was no one there? Wait, something was fluttering back and forth just below my line of sight.
“Over here, pyon. My name is Usaunny, pyon.”
There, a rabbit wearing a Santa hat was waving a stick… around to get my attention.
“Nice to meet you, pyon.”
“Oh, uh. Nice to meet you too, Usaunny.”

Oh, is that it? A Beastman—since this is another world, maybe races like this exist here. After all, I know absolutely nothing about this world, and I only have a rough idea of what the Book of the Four Holy Weapons is about.
“You seem to know my name—did someone introduce me?”
“You’ve been the talk of the town, pyon. That’s why I came to say hello, pyon.”
“Oh, is that so?”

It’s only natural that rumors would spread about the Hero’s Gathering of companions, right? Maybe she heard the rumors and came straight to me? Having a rabbit Beastman join my party sounds like a dream… She looks cute, so I’m not sure how effective she’ll be in battle, but she’ll definitely be a source of comfort. As I watch Ms. Usaunny, I notice her nose twitching. Her ears are laid back too… Oh, I feel like she’s striking a pose—or maybe it’s just the angle—that makes her look especially cute. The way she tilts her head slightly and clasps her hands together is really endearing. Without thinking, I gently stroke her cheek, and she squints her eyes in pleasure.
“Ehehe… pyon. You can pet me some more, pyon.”
“Well, I’ll take you up on that.”
So, I let myself pet her a little more.
“Mufufu… that tickles, pyon.”
Her fur is so fluffy—she’s just like a stuffed animal, so cute. After petting her just a little more, Usaunny stepped back a bit, then tilted her head and asked,
“I have a question for you—Naofumi-kun, pyon.”
But—is it just my imagination, or does Usaunny’s voice sound familiar? It’s just my imagination, right?
“What is it?”
I wonder what this cute Usaunny wants to ask me? Honestly, I’m the one who knows next to nothing about this world.
“Oto—Naofumi-kun, what do you think about fate, pyon?”
“Fate, huh… Maybe it’s this wonderful series of events I’m experiencing right now?”

You know… having a person who looks like a talking animal come up to you and pet you in such a cute way—isn’t that a wonderful experience? I’m currently having this strange experience that’s a mix of excitement and comfort, so that’s why I answered that way. The experience of petting a Beastman in this dreamlike, impossible situation is truly precious. Well, sure, you can pet animals like neighborhood dogs and cats, or animals at petting zoos and pet shops. If you call it fate that I get to pet Usaunny-san, who came all the way just to see me, isn’t that a wonderful thing?
“Then let me ask you again, hop.”
“What?”
“Which would you prefer: something stimulating or something not? In the future, would you like to experience the kind of stimulation that would make you kick me away, hop?”
“Huh?”
Man… what kind of stimulating experience would kicking the cute Usaunny-san away even be? I’d really rather not have that kind of experience, if I can help it.
“That kind of excitement might be a bit much… I’d rather have fun with everyone, while still feeling a sense of excitement.”

After all, I have to gather my friends and take on the “Wave” disaster. I don’t quite grasp the full extent of the damage yet, but I have to be ready to fight when the time comes. Since all I can do is protect others, having allies is essential.
“Understood, Pyong. Well then, I’ll take my leave for now, Pyong. Oto—Naofumi-kun. Good night, pyon.”
“Ah… yeah. Good night.”
I wonder what kind of question that was? I can’t shake this lingering feeling that I might have given the wrong answer… With that thought in mind, I watched Usaunny leave.
“…Maybe I should have asked her to join me?”

Or maybe if I see a girl like that at the tavern, I should try striking up a conversation. As a “healer,” I guess. Well, I do wonder if it’s a good idea to recruit a healer out of the blue, though. Should I prioritize combat strength first, after all? If this were a video game, wouldn’t it be safer to hire a swordsman or someone for the front lines? I should’ve asked Ren and Itsuki about the standard party compositions in this world. They seemed to know a lot about it. Motoyasu was friendly enough, but I don’t think he ever brought up that kind of topic, did he? I wonder if he’s actually familiar with this world, too? He did mention something about being stabbed by some mean woman who forced him into a double suicide, though. With those thoughts running through my mind—and wondering if I was coming across as a bit of a country bumpkin—I hid my money and went to bed early.
Hmm… I feel like I hear some rustling nearby—maybe it’s the room next door…? Clink, clink… It’s hot in here… My clothes are sticking to me.

I kind of think I heard a voice… or was it just my imagination? Also, I thought I heard a tapping sound coming from the ceiling. I’ve heard that kind of sound before—like mice running across the roof—at a relative’s house in the countryside. Since this is another world, it wouldn’t be strange if there were mice around here.
Sway, sway…
“Oooh—Naofumi-kun. I want you to wake up, pyon.”
Ugh… just five more minutes…
“I’d like you to wake up, pyon. Otherwise, I’ll burrow under the covers, pyon.”
Squirm, squirm……
“Mufufu…… I’m sleeping next to my Father, pyon.”
……Hmm? Something moving pokes its head out onto my chest while I’m asleep. When I open my eyes, the room is still dark. As I squint, wondering what’s going on……
“Excuse me for disturbing you while you’re sleeping, pyon.”
“Whoa!”
For some reason, Usaunny was peeking out from inside my bed and greeting me. When did she start sleeping next to me!? Did she crawl into my bed while I was asleep?
“U-Usaunny!? What are you doing in my bed while I’m asleep!?”
“O—I saw a thief leaving Naofumi-kun’s room, so I chased after him and got it back, Pyon. I called out to you several times, but you didn’t wake up, so I let myself in, Pyon.”
“Huh!?”
I jumped out of bed in a panic and checked my money pouch—Usaunny held it out to me. I checked the contents… yeah. Everything’s fine.
“They’d also stolen some equipment and clothes, so I retrieved those too, Pyon.”
“Ah, thank you.”
It seems Usaunny managed to get various items back from the thief—what a relief.
“It seems this inn is a dangerous place that’s in cahoots with thieves, Pyon. It’s dangerous, so I’d like you to come with me, Pyon.”
“Being told that out of the blue… Well, okay, I get it.”

Even though I’d locked the door, the fact that someone managed to open it and enter my room means it wouldn’t be surprising if such activities were actually taking place here. Even if it was a misunderstanding, leaving the lodging fee in the room should be fine, and I can always report this inn—and its criminal activities—to the kingdom and the king later, right?
“Come on, I want you to hold my spear with me, Pyon. If we do this, no one will spot us, Pyon.”
“Okay.”
So, after leaving the room with the lodging fee behind, I was led out of the inn by Mr. Usaunny. And when we stepped out of the inn… there were quite a few soldiers patrolling the area.
“They’re probably sleeping soundly right about now.”
“What a bunch of idiots.”
They’re pointing at the inn with their thumbs and grinning… that makes a really bad impression. I guess soldiers really are a rough bunch, huh?
“…Guilty, Pyong.”
“Usaunny?”
At the sound of my voice, Ms. Usaunny twitched her ears and turned around with a smile.
“Let’s go, pyon.”
“Okay.”

So, we left the inn… and a little while later, Usaunny sent me a message through the system. A party invite? Oh, she’s adding me to her party. Hmm, so that’s how you form parties in this world. I accepted.
“Then, let’s move a bit, pyon.”
“Huh? Okay.”
Suddenly, I felt a sense of floating, and the scenery changed. Looking around, I saw a grassland…? It seemed we’d been teleported outside the castle town of Melromarc.
“Whoa.”
“We traveled via a portal, Pyon.”
“Wow… so you can do that, too?”

I don’t know if it’s Magic or what, but it really feels like another world. To think we could travel this far so effortlessly. So, even though I was a bit sleepy, I headed to the nearby forest with Usaunny and enjoyed a night of camping… or rather, sleeping under the stars.
The next morning. When Usaunny and I headed to a place called Rafan Village—which I’d planned to visit based on a map of the area—...
“Everyone! Search thoroughly!”
“Where is it!?”
It seemed like soldiers and all sorts of people were running around frantically. I wonder what’s going on?
“Are you curious, Pyon?”
“Yeah. Do you know, Usaunny?”
“I can hear it in my ear, Pyon. It says we can’t track down the three heroes, so we need to go look for them, Pyon.”
“Three…”
Since I’m being led around by Ms. Usaunny myself, does that mean I’m one of the heroes whose whereabouts are unknown?
“For the heroes to suddenly vanish like this! Could it be that the Shield Demon and those Beastmen have beaten us to it!?”
“We’ve also heard reports that someone who tried to strip the Shield of his clothes was attacked by someone… Could that be true?”

The Shield… demon? The term “Beastman” sounded like it carried a lot of negative connotations. Come to think of it, why is it that when I’m with Usaunny, those guys don’t seem to even notice us? “Stripped of his clothes”… that reminds me of what Usaunny said last night about a burglar breaking into my room. Surely not… right?
Feeling a bit uneasy about that… I left the village to have a late breakfast and was cooking over a campfire in the woods when—
“Oh, isn’t that Naofumi Iwatani, the so-called Shield Hero? Sniff, sniff… that smells good. Would you mind letting me have some of that food too?”
A beastman wearing a Santa hat and carrying a sword that looked like a Siberian Husky puppy approached me. His delivery sounded a bit wooden, though…
“His name is Inult, pyon. He’s my companion, pyon.”
“Is that so? Since you’re here, would you like to eat some?”
I’d been making skewers with the meat from the monster Usaunny had defeated, so I handed one to Inult.
“Hmph, I’ll take it.”
Inult took it and began eating the skewered meat, looking a bit hesitant.
“Mm… not bad.”
Inult kept eating, looking as if he couldn’t quite bring himself to admit it.
“Alright, that’s good enough. As a thank-you for the meal, I’ll tag along.”
“Oh, yeah. Thanks.”
“You’re leaving this country, right?”
“Huh? Is that so?”
When I asked Usaunny, she nodded.

“This is a bad country—one that’s been hiding all sorts of things from Naofumi-kun, pyon. So I’ll see you off, pyon. Inult, if you’re going to help him leave the country, I’ll let you eat as much as you want, pyon.”
“Hey, don’t get so high and mighty… ahem. That’s what he’s saying.”
Weren’t they talking behind my back? Usaunny and Inult joined me, both looking rather suspicious.
“The Demon of the Shield has gone into hiding and is on the run. Anyone who recognizes this face, report it immediately!”

The very next morning, I happened to see a scene where wanted posters—complete with a sketch and photo that looked just like me—were being distributed. As I was being led along by Usaunny and the others, I got the feeling that things were taking a… bad turn.
“…So it turned out just as I said it would.”
“Inult, do you know something?”
“…Nope?”
I was walking down the highway, wondering why he was acting like he knew something but wouldn’t say it, when…
“‘“The Demon of the Shield and those Beastmen! Kill them now!”’”
“Whoa!”
“I won’t let you! Pyon! Tou!”
With that, Usaunny charged bravely and fiercely at the group that had turned their killing intent toward me, taking them all down.
“Hmph…”
Inult was also holding back the ones who’d come running. Whoa… they’re targeting me with arrows and Magic.
“Ugh…”
“Damn… how stupid…”
“To be taken down by Beastmen…”
Thanks to Usaunny, every single one of the attackers who’d come after me was knocked down.
“You get it now, right? It seems this country wants to make you out to be the villain, so we’re going to take you to a safe place. Just shut up and follow us.”
“Ugh…”
“That attitude—you’re still skeptical, aren’t you? Listen up. In this country, there are nobles who’ll torture and torment any Demi-Human, even a young girl.”
Inult furrowed his brow and gave me a warning look. Then he glanced over at Usaunny too… I wonder what’s up with that?

I’d find out later, but apparently, Inult—no, Ren—had been taken to see the people torturing a young girl the same night Motoyasu—Usaunny—came to check on me. After being forced to watch a burglar break into my room, he was taken to witness the country’s inner workings alongside Itsuki. Of course, they say they rescued the girl and placed her in a safe location. However, back then, I had no idea about any of that and was simply enjoying watching Usaunny and the others interact.
“Well… I’m hungry.”
“You just ate a little while ago, didn’t you?”
Inult’s phrasing sounds a bit like he’s acting. You wouldn’t get hungry after dealing with a bunch of people who are trying to kill me.
“Let’s make bell-shaped castella, pyon!”
Out of nowhere, Usaunny had procured ingredients like flour and was urging me to get started.
“Why bell castella…?”
Well, since Usaunny was using Magic to provide the heat, we were casually making some bell castella.
“Sniff, sniff. That smells delicious. Ah… that must be Naofumi-san over there. I’ve heard the rumors. Please, could I have one of those millet dumplings—”
“It’s bell castella, you know.”

Some kind of squirrel beastman wearing a Santa hat and holding a bow… a child about the same age as Usaunny-san and the others wandered over in a somewhat theatrical tone and spoke to me. When Inult-san explained the situation, the child quickly grabbed Inult-san’s arm, moved away, and started whispering.
“Hey, this isn’t what we planned, is it?”
“He’s the one who suddenly said ‘Bell Castella.’”
“Seriously…”
“Father. Please pet me, pyooon!”

Maybe I should just ignore the fact that Usaunny has started calling me “Father.” She’s cute, sure… but honestly, when this over-the-top acting goes on for this long, it really starts to bug me. What on earth have I gotten myself mixed up in?
“Her name is Riska, pyoon. She’s the glutton of the group, pyoon.”
“Hey! Don’t make up weird character traits like that!　Who’s the glutton?!”
Looks like they don’t get along very well.
“Oh well, do you want some too?”
I made a large bell-shaped castella on a skewer and tried to hand it to the little squirrel.
“Time for a little trick, hop!”

With a swift motion, Usaunny fiddled with the bell-shaped castella… carving out the ears, nose, and eyes with the tip of the skewer to finish it off. The result was a bell castella that looked exactly like Riska-san.
“Hey, Moto—Usaunny-san!”
“It’s a Riska-castella, pyon!”
“Huh, it really does look just like her.”
“E—Inult-san, what are you saying?!”
Somehow, a cute little argument between these mascots was unfolding right before my eyes. In the end, Riska ate the bell-shaped castella, which they’d dubbed “Riska-stera.”
“It doesn’t taste half bad. Anyway, this is a thank-you gift for the food. I’ll be coming along with you. I look forward to traveling with you from now on.”
“Ah, yeah.”

I could tell these kids were putting on a show, but what on earth were they trying to accomplish? As I continued my journey with Usaunny and the others… it was decided that Riska would stay behind with me while Usaunny and the others went off on a hunting trip.
Then…
“Neigh-neigh!”
A horse with a… rather unusual neigh is approaching us as we camp.
“That sounded like a pretty unusual neigh, if I’m not mistaken…”
“Neigh, neigh.”

It’s making a sound that sounds just like a horse—I mean, it’s a wild horse… right? But it comes right up to me and sits down quietly. It seems pretty used to people. Maybe it’s an abandoned horse? It doesn’t seem to have a saddle or anything, though. Oh, I should be able to tell its monster name just by looking, so let me check.
Horse?

Why is it in the interrogative form? Is it because my level is low? Anyway, the horse is staring intently at me. I recognize those eyes—the horses at petting farms that let people ride them had gentle eyes just like this. So I gently reach out to touch it.
The horse doesn’t resist or show any signs of displeasure; it just stays calm. So when I stroke it, it squints its eyes as if it feels good.
“Um, I have a brush I got from Usaunny, so let’s use this to tidy up its coat a bit.”
“So you’ve already been issued one, huh?”

By the way, Riska-san said she was hungry and asked for food, so I made some Smoked Meat for her to eat. She also asked for stir-fried vegetables, so I’m preparing those over the campfire right now. And just like that, I even managed to brush the horse.
“Brr.”
It seemed as if it was saying, “Go ahead and ride me,” so I climbed onto its back, and the horse stood up with a thump.
“Is it really okay to just hop on a wild horse like that?”
“I think it’s fine? I mean, sure, there might be things like kelpies around in another world.”
“Kelpies?”

“Yeah. Don’t you know about them, Riska? They’re monsters that subtly lure people onto their backs—either by letting them ride or by suddenly plunging into the water to drown them and eat their innards. Some say they’ll latch onto you just by touching them.”
“Isn’t this getting a little too serious to laugh about?”
“I think it’s fine. This one’s pretty docile.”
“Neigh-neigh,”

The horse was trotting along without any trouble. Hmm, if it’s this used to people, it’d make the trip a lot easier if I could just ride it as is. Just as I was playfully teasing the horse with Riska… thud! Usaunny came stomping over with Inult-san and dropped what looked like a monster—a gift, perhaps.
“Father, what on earth are you doing?”
“What do you mean? A wild horse took a liking to me, so I’m just riding on its back.”
“Hey! Get off my Father right now! Even if you try to hide it, the smell will give you away in a heartbeat!”

Usaunny looked pretty flustered as he swung his spear around wildly and came charging toward us. I’m not hopping around, Usaunny. Are you… losing the composure to add those little exclamations at the end of your sentences?
“Neigh!”
“Whoa!?”
Just then, it leaped high into the air… no, not a leap—wings suddenly sprouted from the horse’s back, and it soared upward.
“Why on earth are you here, you wretch!? I mean, ‘Pyon’!”
“Oh… what’s that? Do you know him?”
“He’s flying, Naofumi-san. Are you okay?”
“Well, he looks fine, but could you help me out?”
“Don’t worry. I won’t let Naofumi get hurt. I’m just reading the room and saying hello.”
“Don’t listen to him! Father, you mustn’t ride that thing!”
“Heh heh heh, I’ve given Naofumi a ride.”

And so, the talking horse… no, wait—its form gradually shifted, and a dragon was now having a conversation with Usaunny while glaring at him. It seems he knows who I am, and he doesn’t get along with Usaunny-san. Is he… not an enemy?
“It looks like we’re on our way somewhere. My name is Gaelion. I’ll help you out.”
“Ah, thank you, Gaelion-san. Do you know Usaunny-san?”
“I’d like you to call me Gaelion-chan. Hmm, as for Usaunny… I’ve been asked to look after her.”

Huh… is that so? It doesn’t seem like they get along very well—or rather, Usaunny really seems to dislike him—but I guess he’s her guardian? Gaelion-chan, who had been flying, slowly landed on the ground and set me down.
“Travel is better with company; it’s nice to have some liveliness. I’ll protect you.”
“Thanks. Apparently, we’re leaving this country to go to a safe place—a place called the Beastmen’s Kingdom.”
“I see. So we’re heading to the eastern kingdom, Siltvelt.”
Oh, is that right?
“Or are we going to Shieldfreeden? Gaelion knows a lot about that one, too. Well, if Naofumi’s going there, I can’t really recommend it unless he gets a little stronger first.”
“I don’t really get the difference.”
I mean, I don’t know much about this world anyway.
“You’ll learn as you go.”
“I’m the one who’s supposed to teach my Father, Pyon! Don’t go blabbing everything, Pyon!”

Anyway, our group is getting livelier and livelier as more members join… It really feels like a dream. I mean, there’s Usaunny and the others, right? Plus, none of them—including Gaelion—are human. Ah, it really feels like another world—it’s so exciting.
“Sigh…”

Well, the problem is that every now and then we get hassled by these guys in full armor who look like soldiers—they attack us, screaming, “You Shield Hero! Dieeeeeeeeeee!” and radiating murderous intent. They even shouted stuff like, “I’ll never let you escape this country!” Hmm… How is it that people are the scary ones, after all? Apparently, the country of Melromarc is pretty barbaric. The trope where the country that summons you is “evil” has been a classic in anime for ages—I guess this fits that mold too. As for the rest… was it a fortress deep in the mountains? After passing through an empty fortress where there wasn’t a single soul in sight, it seems we left the country of Melromarc. Gaelion-chan was exasperated with Usaunny-san, who insisted the fortress was safe, saying, “You did it again, didn’t you?” I wonder what happened there? Anyway, Usaunny-san raised a monster called a Filolial and started using it as a vehicle to carry everyone around.
“Hey, Rival! Father’s going to give Yuki-chan a ride, so move it, hop!”
“I don’t want to.”
“Ugh…”
“By the way… since the one trying to get on right now is Yuki, does that mean it’s Filo again this time?”
“Of course it is, pyon!”
“That guy’s here anyway, so you can’t touch him. Don’t you think it’d be nice to ride Sakura for a change?”
“Ugh…”
“If you try to get back at him too much, he’ll just use *that* thing to harass you again. Do you really want that? It’s all because of Filo, you know.”
“Ugh… Don’t remind me, pyon…”

They’re having a conversation only Usaunny and the others would understand. Is “Filo” some kind of term? Is “Sakura” about the flower? When Gaelion-chan travels along the highway, she turns into a horse and gives me a ride.
“You two are arguing again, aren’t you?”
“You do that a lot.”
Riska and Inult seemed to have gotten used to this back-and-forth and were just rolling their eyes at it. Well… I guess they’re just bickering affectionately?
“Guaaaa!”
“Gua-gua!”
Oh, the Filolials are letting out threatening growls at Gaelion-chan. It seems their species just don’t get along.
“A monster’s appeared. Look, Usaunny, if we don’t take it down first, Gaelion’s going to carry Naofumi on her back and go take it down herself!”
“Tch! That’s right, hop! Yuki-chan, let’s go, hop!”
“Guaa!”
And with that, Usaunny swings her spear around wildly and dashes out to defeat the monster with flair.
“How should I put it… It’s like we’ve stepped right into a fairy tale world.”
“Hmm. That’s one way to look at it.”
“Which fairy tale, specifically?”
Riska-san asks.
“Let’s see… Setting Usaunny-san aside for a moment, Inult-san’s acting made me think, ‘Is this Momotaro?’”
“Ah, I was going for that.”
“I was thinking the same thing. Or am I wrong?”
“If anything, even though the direction’s opposite, isn’t it *Journey to the West*?”
I don’t know if *Journey to the West* even exists in this world, though.
“*Journey to the West*… You’re right, it does kind of look like that. So Son Goku is that guy, and Naofumi-san is Tripitaka?”
“You hit the nail on the head. Tripitaka is Naofumi, the Shield Hero… So the monsters along the way are humans attacking us.”

“Ahaha,” I let out a slightly dry laugh. Yeah. That’s right. There are definitely a lot of moments where I feel like I’m constantly being hassled by people who are out to kill me one way or another. And, needless to say, the “Sun Wukong” you’re referring to is Usaunny, swinging that spear around in battle. His weapon looks the part, too. It almost looks like he’s swinging a staff.
“I hear you, Pyon! I’m Sun Wukong, Pyon. Uki-ki!”
“In that case, are your companions Sha Wujing and Zhu Bajie? I’ll be Sha Wujing, then.”
“Hey, wait—I’m Sha Wujing.”
“What’s that, Ren… Inult-san? Shall I ask why you’re so eager to take Sha Wujing’s role?”
Inult-san and Riska-san start butting heads over the casting.
“When—Riska, don’t you get it? Hey, Naofumi, you get it, right?”
“Ah…”

Riska is still munching away on the food I made. Even though we all just ate together a little while ago. She’s stuffing it into her cheek pouches without even realizing it—she doesn’t seem to have a clue. It’s this slightly absent-minded, comical vibe that makes me think Riska is the perfect fit for Zhu Bajie. Usaunny is the most hot-blooded of the three—she’s the first to rush into battle—so she’s Sun Wukong. Out of the three, Inult-san is the calm one—he’s Sha Wujing—and Riska-san as Zhu Bajie just feels right somehow.
“You’re definitely Zhu Bajie, Riska-san.”
“If you’ve got a complaint, finish eating what’s in your cheek pouches first before you say anything.”
“Huh? Come to think of it, I’ve been noticing the aftertaste of the food lingering forever, but I didn’t realize it! H-h… I’m not giving up the Sha Wujing spot! I don’t want to be Zhu Bajie.”
“Hmm… In the Land of the Stage, Zhu Bajie is actually more popular than Sun Wukong, you know.”
“Really?”
It seems even Riska doesn’t know that.

“Yeah. Part of it is that he has the most human-like background out of the three companions, but it’s also because he was always a diligent monk from the moment he joined the group until the end of the journey. So, he’s actually a serious guy.”
Well, the fact that he ends up playing the gluttonous role after the journey is over is probably just part of his role as the comic relief, but I’ll just keep that to myself.
“It seems Zhu Bajie was the one Sun Wukong teased the most, too.”
“Ah… he definitely gets picked on by Usaunny a lot.”
“That’s such a lousy role!”
“What about Gaelion? I think there was a story about that spread by the hero.”
“Yeah, there is. They say the horse that carried Tripitaka was actually a dragon.”
Come to think of it, the casting feels almost intentional. Gaelion-chan did come closer disguised as a horse, after all. Was she reading the room?
“Guaaah!”
“Father. I did it!”
“You did great, Usaunny.”
“Ehehe, I’d like you to pet me later, pyon. Oh, and please don’t use the brush you used on my Rival to groom me, pyon!”
“Got it.”
“……Father. Is the journey fun, pyon?”
“Yeah.”

Just as she asked, I feel like we’re all having a fun and exciting adventure together. It’s a bit fanciful, but it’s still fun, I guess. I did have that unpleasant experience where not a single companion was arranged by the government, but here I am, traveling with everyone like this.

Finding out that the three of them were actually Motoyasu and the others… well, that’s a story for a little later. Seriously, how did things end up like this…? Still, I won’t deny that traveling with the heroes was a lot of fun. Many more events would unfold from here on out, and we’d end up facing the waves threatening the world.
